missing_data_treatment: inputs gated to physical ranges pre-binning; index computed only where TMP+DPT+RH valid; full basin rectangle, no shoreline cut; missing analysis transparent; never zero-filled; corroborated visibility density outranks risk, dry-air speckles never paint active fog.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.

legend_scale_html: Fog index 0-100 (DERIVED from HRRR analysis, fixed absolute scale): 0 No observed fog sage green → 20 Fog risk yellow-green (risk owns 0-35: thermodynamic base x calm-air factor) → 40 Active fog gold (VIS 4797 m / 2.98 mi) → 60 Active fog brick red (VIS 3486 m / 2.17 mi) → 80 Active fog violet (VIS 1842 m / 1.14 mi) → 100 Active fog deep purple (VIS 0 m). Active fog by corroborated density owns 35-100 (gate: VIS below 5000 m with RH at/above 90%); dry-air speckles can never paint active fog. Same index always shows the same color — not a copy of the visibility layer.

stats.derivation: v2: risk r = rh_factor*spread_factor*calm_factor in [0,1] (rh_factor=clip((RH-70)/30,0,1); spread_factor=clip((3-S)/3,0,1), S=TMP-DPT C deg; calm_factor=clip((6-wspd)/6,0.35,1)) -> risk zone 35*r. Corroborated density d = clip((5000-VIS)/5000,0,1)^0.8 only where VIS<5000m & RH>=90 -> fog zone 35+65*d. Index = max of the two (continuous at VIS=5000m). Risk owns 0-35, active fog by density owns 35-100. Distinct from raw visibility; dry-air speckles can never paint active fog.

A derived fog-risk index from operational HRRR analysis: low greens mark clear air, yellows and oranges mark elevated fog risk from saturated calm air, and reds into deep purple mark active fog confirmed by collapsed visibility. Built for Great Lakes navigation, shoreline conditions, aviation awareness, and nighttime environmental monitoring. Derivation: v2: risk r = rh_factor*spread_factor*calm_factor in [0,1] (rh_factor=clip((RH-70)/30,0,1); spread_factor=clip((3-S)/3,0,1), S=TMP-DPT C deg; calm_factor=clip((6-wspd)/6,0.35,1)) -> risk zone 35*r. Corroborated density d = clip((5000-VIS)/5000,0,1)^0.8 only where VIS<5000m & RH>=90 -> fog zone 35+65*d. Index = max of the two (continuous at VIS=5000m). Risk owns 0-35, active fog by density owns 35-100. Distinct from raw visibility; dry-air speckles can never paint active fog.

Fog science (boundary-layer meteorology and aerosol microphysics) studies saturation, radiative cooling, and droplet nucleation that reduce visibility below one kilometer. Radiation fog forms over land and calm water on clear nights; advection and steam fog form where air-water temperature contrasts drive lake-effect events. The index separates fog likelihood from raw visibility so developing risk reads before, and active fog reads during, an event.

Units: fog index 0-100 (display; derived, see derivation)
